In-scope systems.value: GL trial balance feeds the SFR forms; CSR/BSCR schedules built in the BMA ERICA e-filing template workbook

Compliance procedure documented.value: Bermuda SFR/CSR Preparation Procedure — schedule-by-schedule owner map, GL-to-form tie-out, BSCR input lineage, ERICA upload and lock steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the CFO; refreshed each year when the BMA publishes the new CSR handbook and ERICA schema

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: SFR + CSR due to the BMA within four months of financial year-end (30 April for a 31 December year-end); any BMA-granted extension letter logged against the entry

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10 days before 30 April to the Controller, Statutory Reporting Manager and Appointed Actuary

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed SFR/CSR PDFs, ERICA submission receipts, GL tie-out workpapers and BSCR support retained at the principal office for at least five years per the Insurance Returns and Solvency Regulations 1980

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late schedules, ERICA validation failures and post-filing restatements logged with root cause and BMA correspondence attached

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off any late or amended Bermuda return before it is re-lodged with the BMA

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any schedule was filed after the statutory deadline without a BMA extension, or any filed figure differs from the audited GL by more than a rounding difference

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual test performed within 60 days of the 30 April filing, covering that year's return end-to-end

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit tests; no tester may have prepared or reviewed any filed schedule

Regulator-ready documentation.value: ERICA submission receipts, signed SFR forms, BSCR model output and GL reconciliations producible to the BMA within 5 business days of a s.18 request

checklist.step: Open the annual SFR/CSR cycle and confirm the statutory deadline
actions: Create the year's Bermuda filing record with entity name, registration class (3A/3B/4), financial year-end and the s.17 due date four months after year-end (30 April for 31 December).
Download the current-year Capital and Solvency Return handbook and ERICA schedule templates from the BMA website (bma.bm ▸ Regulatory Filings) and diff them against last year's forms.
Circulate the schedule-owner map — each SFR form, CSR schedule and BSCR exhibit assigned to a named preparer with an internal due date at least 20 business days before 30 April.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary whether any extension request under s.17(3) is needed and, if so, draft it for BMA submission before the original deadline.
checklist.done: the filing record shows class, statutory due date, current-year templates and a named owner per schedule.

checklist.step: Freeze the trial balance and map the GL to the statutory forms
actions: Extract the final post-close trial balance for the Bermuda entity from the GL and lock the period so no late entries move the filed numbers.
Run the GL-to-SFR mapping workbook line by line: each SFR Form 1/2/8 caption (assets, liabilities, statutory capital and surplus, income) must trace to named GL accounts.
Reconcile total statutory assets and total capital and surplus to the audited financial statements draft from the external auditor and document every reconciling item.
Hand unmapped or new GL accounts to the Senior Accountant for classification before any form is populated.
checklist.done: every SFR caption traces to locked GL accounts and the capital and surplus figure reconciles to the audit draft.

checklist.step: Prepare the statutory balance sheet and income forms
actions: Populate the SFR statutory balance sheet and statutory statement of income in the ERICA template workbook from the mapped trial balance.

Apply the statutory admissibility rules from the Insurance Account Rules — deduct non-admitted assets (unquoted affiliates, prepaid expenses beyond limits) and record each deduction on the adjustments tab.
Compute statutory capital and surplus and compare it to the entity's minimum margin of solvency (MSM) and to the class minimum paid-up share capital.
Pass the completed forms to the Statutory Reporting Manager with the adjustments tab for review.
checklist.done: statutory forms are populated, every non-admitted adjustment is itemised, and capital and surplus clears the MSM.

checklist.step: Build the loss reserve and technical provision schedules
actions: Export gross and net loss and loss expense provisions by statutory line from the reserving platform as at year-end.
Populate the SFR loss reserve schedules and the CSR technical provision exhibits, splitting case reserves, IBNR and the risk margin per the BMA's EBS technical provisions guidance.
Tie opening balances to last year's filed return and explain movements above 10% per line in the schedule commentary.
Deliver the schedules to the Appointed Actuary for the s.26 loss reserve opinion linkage.
checklist.done: reserve schedules tie to the reserving platform and prior filed return, with movement commentary attached.

checklist.step: Run the BSCR model and complete the capital schedules
actions: Load year-end asset, premium, reserve and catastrophe inputs into the BMA's BSCR model workbook for the entity's class.
Run the model and record the Enhanced Capital Requirement (ECR), the MSM and the Target Capital Level (120% of ECR) on the CSR capital summary.
Trace every BSCR input cell back to the GL extract, investment schedules or cat model output and file the lineage tab with the workbook.
Flag to the Capital Management Manager any coverage ratio below internal appetite so a capital action can be considered before filing.
checklist.done: the BSCR workbook produces ECR/MSM/TCL figures with a complete input lineage tab and the coverage ratio is known.

checklist.step: Prepare the Economic Balance Sheet (EBS) exhibits
actions: Revalue assets and liabilities on the EBS basis prescribed in the Prudential Standards Rules — fair-value assets, best-estimate technical provisions plus risk margin discounted on the BMA yield curves.
Download the year-end BMA discount curves from the BMA website and evidence the curve version used in the workpaper.
Complete the EBS schedules in the CSR and reconcile EBS capital and surplus to statutory capital and surplus with a bridging table.
Have the Appointed Actuary review and initial the EBS bridging table.
checklist.done: EBS exhibits are complete on the published BMA curves with a reviewed statutory-to-EBS bridge.

checklist.step: Complete the remaining CSR qualitative and quantitative schedules
actions: Populate the CSR schedules for intra-group transactions, reinsurance counterparty exposures, investment concentrations, catastrophe risk and eligible capital tiering, pulling counterparty data from the ceded reinsurance analyst's treaty listing.
Draft the qualitative schedule narratives (risk management, governance, outsourcing) with the Enterprise Risk Manager and keep them consistent with the ORSA/CISSA submission.
Cross-check schedule totals against the statutory forms — reinsurance recoverables, investments and capital must agree across every schedule.
Log completion of each schedule against the owner map in the filing tracker.
checklist.done: every CSR schedule is complete, internally consistent with the SFR forms, and marked done in the tracker.

checklist.step: Obtain the Appointed Actuary's opinion and the actuarial sign-offs
actions: Review the filed reserve schedules and issue the signed loss reserve opinion required with the SFR for the entity's class.
Confirm the opinion wording matches the BMA's prescribed form and covers gross and net provisions as stated on the schedules.
Deliver the signed opinion PDF to the Statutory Reporting Manager for inclusion in the ERICA upload package.
Record any qualification or caveat in the filing tracker and brief the CFO on it before signing week.
checklist.done: a signed, unqualified (or CFO-briefed) actuarial opinion in the prescribed form sits in the filing package.

checklist.step: Prepare the Declaration of Compliance under s.8A
actions: Draft the s.8A Declaration of Compliance confirming the insurer has complied with the minimum criteria, solvency margin and applicable Act requirements for the year.
Circulate the declaration through the board portal for signature by two directors (or a director and the principal representative) as the Act prescribes.
Collect any exceptions raised by signatories, route them to the Head of Compliance for resolution, and re-circulate if wording changes.
File the signed declaration into the ERICA package and minute the approval.
checklist.done: a signed Declaration of Compliance is in the filing package and its approval is minuted.

checklist.step: Run the pre-filing quality review and lock the package
actions: Re-perform the top-level tie-outs: statutory capital and surplus consistent across SFR forms, CSR summary, BSCR output and EBS bridge.
Run the ERICA validation rules on the draft upload and clear every validation error or warning with the schedule owner.
Walk the CFO through the capital position, coverage ratio and any judgement calls in a signing meeting and capture the CFO's approval by email.
Lock the workbook versions and archive the as-filed drafts so post-filing edits are impossible without a new version.
checklist.done: validations pass, tie-outs agree, CFO approval is captured and the package is version-locked.

checklist.step: File the SFR and CSR through the BMA ERICA portal by the deadline
actions: Log in to the BMA's ERICA e-filing portal with the entity's filer credentials and open the current-year Statutory Financial Return submission.
Upload the SFR forms, CSR schedules, BSCR workbook, actuarial opinion and Declaration of Compliance against the correct filing slots, checking each attachment opens cleanly after upload.
Submit before the four-month deadline (30 April), download the ERICA submission confirmation receipt and save it with a timestamp.
Notify the Controller, CFO and Regulatory Reporting Manager that the filing is lodged, quoting the ERICA reference.
checklist.done: ERICA shows the return submitted on or before the deadline and the receipt is archived with its reference.

checklist.step: Pay the annual BMA fee and complete companion lodgements
actions: Confirm the annual registration fee for the entity's class was paid to the BMA by the 31 March statutory due date and attach the payment confirmation to the filing record.
Lodge the Financial Condition Report with the SFR and diarise its public disclosure obligation (publication within 14 days of filing) to the owner of item C18.
Check whether any schedule triggers a separate notification (e.g. a material intra-group transaction) and route it to Regulatory Counsel.
Update the filing tracker entry to 'Filed — awaiting BMA acknowledgement'.
checklist.done: fee payment is evidenced, companion lodgements are routed, and the tracker reflects the filed status.

checklist.step: Answer BMA follow-up queries on the return
actions: Log every BMA query letter or email on the return in the filing tracker with its response due date.
Draft responses from the archived workpapers — never recompute filed figures informally — and have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes an error.
Where a correction is required, prepare the amended schedule, obtain CFO sign-off and resubmit through ERICA as an amended filing with a cover note.
Close the query in the tracker with the BMA's acknowledgement attached.
checklist.done: every BMA query has a logged, counsel-cleared response and any amendment is CFO-approved and re-lodged.

checklist.step: Archive the full filing evidence set
actions: File the as-submitted SFR/CSR package, ERICA receipts, tie-out workpapers, BSCR lineage tab, signed opinion and declaration into the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C17 and the filing year.
Apply the five-year retention label required by the Insurance Returns and Solvency Regulations 1980, measured from the filing date.
Verify the principal office can retrieve the set — the s.18 production duty falls there — by testing retrieval from the Bermuda office share.
Index the record by entity, year and ERICA reference.
checklist.done: the complete filing set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable from the principal office.

checklist.step: Hold the post-filing lessons-learned and update the procedure
actions: Review the cycle against the owner map: late schedules, ERICA validation failures and rework logged with root cause.
Update the Bermuda SFR/CSR Preparation Procedure for any BMA handbook change announced for next year and re-approve it with the CFO.
Feed structural issues (chronic late feeds, model input gaps) into the exception log with owners and dates.
Set next year's cycle-open date in the filing calendar.
checklist.done: the procedure is updated and re-approved, and every cycle defect has an owner in the exception log.

testing.step: Build the population of required Bermuda schedules for the year
actions: List every SFR form, CSR schedule and BSCR exhibit required for the entity's class from the current-year BMA CSR handbook — the handbook, not the filing tracker, defines completeness.
Add companion items: actuarial opinion, Declaration of Compliance, FCR lodgement and the 31 March fee payment.
Reconcile the list to what ERICA shows as submitted and to the internal owner map; any handbook-required schedule absent from either is an immediate exception.
testing.done: a handbook-derived schedule population is reconciled to the ERICA submission with gaps listed.

testing.step: Verify filing timeliness against the statutory deadline
actions: Open the archived ERICA submission receipt and read the submission timestamp.
Recompute the s.17 deadline as financial year-end plus four months and compare; where an extension was relied on, sight the BMA extension letter and check the extended date instead.
Confirm the annual fee payment date was on or before 31 March from the payment confirmation.
Log any late submission as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: submission and fee timestamps are verified against recomputed statutory deadlines.

testing.step: Reconcile filed figures to the audited general ledger
actions: Independently extract the locked year-end trial balance and re-run the GL-to-SFR mapping for total assets, total liabilities and statutory capital and surplus.
Compare to the figures on the as-filed SFR forms; any difference beyond rounding is an exception.
Trace the statutory-to-audited reconciliation and confirm every reconciling item has support.
testing.done: filed headline figures re-derive from the locked GL within rounding, with reconciling items evidenced.

testing.step: Draw a sample of schedules for line-level re-performance
actions: Select the statutory balance sheet, the loss reserve schedule, the eligible capital schedule and two further CSR schedules at random (seeded, reproducible).
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
For each sampled schedule, obtain the preparer's workpaper and the source extract it claims to be built from.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering capital, reserves and two random schedules is documented with sources.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled schedules from source data
actions: Rebuild each sampled schedule from the source extract without reference to the filed version, applying the admissibility and classification rules in the Insurance Account Rules.
Compare the rebuilt schedule to the as-filed schedule cell by cell and list every difference.
For the loss reserve schedule, agree gross and net provisions back to the reserving platform export and to the signed actuarial opinion amounts.
testing.done: each sampled schedule re-derives from source or every difference is explained and dispositioned.

testing.step: Recompute the BSCR capital figures
actions: Re-run the filed BSCR workbook from the archived input set and confirm the ECR, MSM and TCL match the filed CSR summary.
Spot-trace ten BSCR input cells to GL, investment or cat-model source via the lineage tab; a missing lineage entry is an exception.
Recompute the coverage ratio (statutory capital and surplus ÷ ECR) and confirm it matches what was reported to the CFO at signing.
The re-performer must not have built the original model run.
testing.done: ECR/MSM/TCL and the coverage ratio reproduce from archived inputs with lineage intact.

testing.step: Verify sign-offs and the Declaration of Compliance
actions: Sight the signed actuarial opinion and confirm the signatory was the BMA-recognised Appointed Actuary for the year.
Sight the s.8A Declaration of Compliance and check the signatories and date precede the ERICA submission.
Confirm the CFO signing-meeting approval email exists and pre-dates submission.
Check the archived package carries the five-year retention label and retrieves from the principal office share.
testing.done: all statutory sign-offs pre-date the filing and the evidence set is retention-labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Trace BMA queries and amendments to closure
actions: Pull every BMA query logged against the return and check each has a counsel-cleared response within its due date.
For any amended filing, confirm CFO sign-off pre-dates the ERICA resubmission and the amendment reason is documented.
Confirm no filed figure was changed outside the amendment process.
testing.done: all queries closed on time with cleared responses, and every amendment is authorised and documented.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception: schedule, what failed (late, mis-stated, unsupported), and regulatory impact under s.17/s.18.
Assign root cause (late feed, mapping error, handbook change missed) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Escalate any late-filing or misstatement finding to the CFO and Regulatory Counsel for a self-report assessment to the BMA.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and — where required — a self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-late/zero-misstatement threshold and write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who prepared no filed schedule — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C17.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the auditor of record holds current BMA approval
actions: Retrieve the BMA approval evidence for the incumbent audit firm and signing partner from the evidence repository and check it names the current entity and remains unrevoked.
Where a new firm or partner is proposed, submit the approval request to the BMA under s.16 with the firm's qualifications before any engagement letter is signed.
Diarise the approval status check at every engagement acceptance so a partner rotation never silently voids approval.
File the current approval evidence against the year's engagement record.
checklist.done: documented, current BMA approval exists for the exact firm and partner engaged for the year.

checklist.step: Take Audit Committee appointment and sign the engagement letter
actions: Table the auditor reappointment (or new appointment) at the Audit Committee with the independence confirmation letter from the firm.
Minute the appointment resolution in the board portal and record any shareholder approval the bye-laws require.
Route the engagement letter — scope covering both statutory statements under s.17 and GAAP statements under s.17A — to the CFO for signature.
File the minuted resolution and signed letter with the engagement record.
checklist.done: the appointment is minuted, independence is confirmed in writing, and a signed engagement letter covers both audit scopes.

checklist.step: Agree the audit timetable back from the 30 April filing deadline
actions: Agree with the audit engagement manager the fieldwork start, review weeks and a signed-opinion delivery date at least 10 business days before 30 April.
Load interim and final fieldwork milestones into the filing calendar with T-60/T-30/T-10 alerts.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's reserve deliverables and the BSCR outputs land before the auditor's reserve testing week.
Circulate the agreed timetable to the Controller, CFO and schedule owners.
checklist.done: a written timetable exists with opinion delivery at least 10 business days before the statutory deadline.

checklist.step: Stand up the PBC list and evidence flow
actions: Load the auditor's prepared-by-client request list into AuditBoard with a named owner and due date per item.
Post each deliverable (trial balance, reconciliations, reserve triangles, investment confirmations, treaty listings) to the secure exchange folder — never by open email.
Chase items at 3 days before due and escalate overdue items to the Controller daily.
Track auditor acceptance of each item so re-requests are visible.
checklist.done: every PBC item is delivered, accepted and traceable in AuditBoard with zero overdue items at fieldwork close.

checklist.step: Coordinate fieldwork and clear audit queries
actions: Hold a weekly status call with the engagement manager during fieldwork and log every open query with an owner and date.
Route reserve and EBS questions to the Appointed Actuary and Valuation Actuary; routing GL questions to the Senior Accountant same-day.
Review proposed audit adjustments with the CFO and book agreed adjustments in the GL before the statutory forms lock.
Record passed (unbooked) adjustments and confirm they stay below the statutory materiality the auditor documents.
checklist.done: fieldwork closes with all queries answered, agreed adjustments booked, and passed adjustments documented as immaterial.

checklist.step: Receive and check the signed audit opinions
actions: Obtain the signed opinion on the statutory financial statements and the signed opinion on the GAAP financial statements from the audit partner.
Check each opinion names the correct legal entity, financial year and framework, and that the signing partner matches the BMA-approved partner.
If any opinion is qualified or carries an emphasis of matter, brief the CFO and Regulatory Counsel the same day and record the agreed handling.
File the signed opinions into the ERICA filing package.
checklist.done: both signed opinions are in the package, partner and entity details verified, and any qualification is escalated in writing.

checklist.step: File the audited statements with the BMA via ERICA
actions: Upload the audited statutory financial statements and the s.17A audited GAAP statements with the SFR submission in the BMA ERICA portal.
Verify each uploaded PDF opens, is signed and is the final version, then submit before the four-month deadline.
Download the ERICA receipt and record the filing date — this date starts the 14-day FCR publication clock.
Notify the Controller, CFO and the FCR owner of the filing date by email the same day.
checklist.done: audited statements are lodged on time and the filing date is communicated as the start of the 14-day clock.

checklist.step: Prepare and approve the Financial Condition Report
actions: Draft the FCR per the Insurance (Public Disclosure) Rules 2015 sections — business and performance, governance structure, risk profile, solvency valuation and capital management — consistent with the filed CSR figures.
Cross-check every number in the FCR against the filed SFR/CSR; no figure may differ from the filing.
Obtain CFO and Chief Risk Officer approval of the draft, then board or delegated-authority approval as the governance framework requires.
Lodge the approved FCR with the BMA alongside the SFR filing.
checklist.done: an approved FCR, numerically consistent with the filed return, is lodged with the BMA.

checklist.step: Publish the FCR within 14 days of filing
actions: Compute the publication deadline as the ERICA filing date plus 14 days and enter it in the filing calendar with day-1 and day-10 alerts.
Send the approved FCR to the Digital Channel Manager for posting on the company website's public disclosures page.
Capture a dated screenshot of the live webpage showing the FCR link and download the posted PDF to prove content identity.
File the screenshot and posted copy as the publication evidence.
checklist.done: the FCR is live on the website within 14 days of filing, evidenced by a dated capture and matching PDF.

checklist.step: Handle any auditor cessation within the statutory window
actions: On any resignation, removal or non-reappointment of the auditor, notify the BMA in writing within 14 days, stating the reason as s.16A requires.
Obtain the outgoing firm's statement of circumstances and file it with the notification.
Start the replacement approval request to the BMA immediately so the entity is never without an approved auditor of record.
Minute the cessation and replacement at the next Audit Committee.
checklist.done: any cessation is notified to the BMA within 14 days and a replacement approval request is in flight.

checklist.step: Track auditor management-letter findings to closure
actions: Load each management-letter finding into AuditBoard with severity, owner and target date agreed with the Controller.
Chase owners monthly and evidence closure with the corrected control artifact, not a narrative assertion.
Report open findings to the Audit Committee quarterly with ageing.
Feed repeat findings into the exception log for root-cause treatment.
checklist.done: every finding has an owner, target date and evidenced closure or a committee-visible ageing status.

checklist.step: Confirm auditor independence and fees annually
actions: Collect the firm's annual independence confirmation and the schedule of audit and non-audit fees.
Check non-audit services against the Audit Committee's pre-approval policy and flag any unapproved service.
Table the independence confirmation and fee schedule at the Audit Committee and minute the conclusion.
File both in the engagement record.
checklist.done: independence is confirmed in writing, fees are pre-approved, and the committee minute records it.

checklist.step: Respond to BMA correspondence on the audited filings
actions: Log each BMA letter or query on the audited statements with its response deadline in the tracker.
Draft responses from the audit file and workpapers, copying the principal representative, and have Regulatory Counsel clear any response conceding a deficiency.
Where the BMA directs a change, agree the remediation plan with the CFO and record it against the query.
Close the tracker item with the BMA acknowledgement attached.
checklist.done: all BMA audit-related queries are logged, cleared, answered on time and closed with acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Archive the engagement evidence set
actions: File the approval evidence, engagement letter, minuted appointment, signed opinions, audited statements, ERICA receipts, FCR and publication capture under REG-057-C18 and the year.
Apply the five-year retention label and verify retrieval from the principal office.
Index by entity, year and audit firm.
checklist.done: the complete engagement set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable.

checklist.step: Debrief the cycle and update the procedure
actions: Review opinion delivery versus the timetable, PBC performance and any near-miss on the 14-day FCR clock with the Controller.
Update the External Audit Coordination Procedure for rule changes (Public Disclosure Rules amendments, BMA guidance) and re-approve it.
Set the next engagement-acceptance date and auditor-approval recheck in the calendar.
Record structural fixes in the exception log with owners.
checklist.done: the procedure is re-approved for the next cycle and every process defect has an owner.

testing.step: Build the population of audit-cycle records for the year
actions: List every Bermuda-registered entity in the group and, for each, the required records: BMA auditor approval, engagement letter, committee minute, two signed opinions, filed audited statements, FCR and publication evidence.
Reconcile the entity list to the BMA registers and to the legal-entity master so no registered entity escapes testing.
Mark any entity missing a required record as an immediate exception.
testing.done: a per-entity record matrix exists, reconciled to the BMA registers, with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Verify the auditor's BMA approval covered the whole year
actions: Sight the BMA approval evidence for the firm and signing partner and check its date range spans the engagement period.
Compare the partner named on the signed opinions to the approved partner; a mismatch is a fail.
Check for any partner rotation or firm change during the year and, if found, sight the fresh approval and the s.16A notification.
testing.done: approval evidence covers the exact firm and partner who signed, for the full engagement period.

testing.step: Verify appointment governance and independence
actions: Read the Audit Committee minute appointing the auditor and check it pre-dates the engagement letter signature.
Sight the written independence confirmation and the non-audit fee schedule against the pre-approval policy.
Flag any non-audit service without pre-approval as an exception to the committee chair.
testing.done: appointment, independence and fee pre-approval are evidenced in the correct sequence.

testing.step: Trace the signed opinions to the filed statements
actions: Open the as-filed ERICA package and confirm both the statutory opinion and the s.17A GAAP opinion are present and signed.
Check entity name, year and framework wording on each opinion against the statements they cover.
Confirm the filed statement PDFs match the final versions in the financial reporting repository byte-for-byte or by document hash.
testing.done: both opinions are in the filed package and the filed statements are the final signed versions.

testing.step: Recompute the filing and FCR publication deadlines
actions: Recompute the four-month s.17 deadline from year-end and compare to the ERICA receipt timestamp.
Recompute the FCR publication deadline as the filing date plus 14 days per the Public Disclosure Rules 2015.
Compare to the dated website capture; publication after day 14 is a fail.
Verify the posted FCR PDF is content-identical to the BMA-lodged version.
testing.done: filing and publication dates fall inside the recomputed statutory windows and the published FCR matches the lodged one.

testing.step: Re-perform the FCR-to-filing number consistency check
actions: Select every quantitative disclosure in the FCR (capital and surplus, ECR, coverage ratio, technical provisions) and trace each to the filed SFR/CSR.
List any figure that differs from the filing, however presented, as an exception.
Check the FCR approval chain (CFO, CRO, board) is evidenced and pre-dates lodgement.
testing.done: every FCR number traces to the filed return and the approval chain pre-dates lodgement.

testing.step: Test audit-adjustment handling
actions: Obtain the auditor's summary of adjusted and passed differences from the Controller's fieldwork file.
Trace each agreed adjustment to a posted GL journal dated before the statutory forms locked.
Confirm passed differences were documented as below statutory materiality and reported to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: agreed adjustments are booked pre-lock and passed differences are documented and committee-reported.

testing.step: Test any auditor cessation notification against the 14-day window
actions: Check the year for any auditor resignation, removal or non-reappointment from committee minutes and the engagement record.
Where one occurred, compute cessation date plus 14 days and compare to the dated BMA notification letter.
Sight the outgoing firm's statement of circumstances and the replacement approval request.
No cessation in the period closes this step as not applicable, stated explicitly.
testing.done: any cessation is proven notified within 14 days, or the step is closed N/A with the evidence searched.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the entity, requirement breached (s.16, s.16A, s.17A or Public Disclosure Rules) and impact.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Escalate lapsed-approval or late-publication findings to the CFO and Regulatory Counsel for a BMA self-report assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner, date and any required self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds (approval lapse, missing opinion, late FCR) and write the conclusion with evidence references.
Sign the workpaper as the independent reviewer segregated from audit coordination.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C18.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Insurance Act 1978 s.18 (production of records), Insurance Returns and Solvency Regulations 1980 (records to be kept), and s.8/s.8B (head office / direction and management in Bermuda), re-read at the annual calendar refresh

In-scope systems.value: Filing calendar and deadline alerts in the regulatory filing tracker; working papers stored in the compliance evidence repository mirrored to the Bermuda principal office share

Compliance procedure documented.value: Bermuda Filing Calendar & Records Retention Procedure — obligation inventory, deadline derivation from the Act and Rules, alert configuration, evidence pack standard and retrieval test

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved on any Insurance Act amendment or BMA rule change affecting deadlines

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: All Bermuda obligations on one calendar: SFR/CSR by year-end + 4 months, annual fee by 31 March, FCR publication filing + 14 days, s.8A declaration with the SFR, event-driven notifications with their statutory windows

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker alerts at T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10/T-1 per calendar entry, routed to the named filing owner and the Regulatory Reporting Manager as backstop

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off closure of any calendar gap or retention failure

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual filing-calendar and retention test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C19

checklist.step: Build the Bermuda obligation inventory from the Act, not from memory
actions: Read the Insurance Act 1978, the Insurance Returns and Solvency Regulations 1980 and the entity's registration conditions, and list every recurring and event-driven obligation with its section reference.
For each obligation record: filer entity, statutory deadline rule (e.g. year-end + 4 months; filing + 14 days; 31 March), owner role and evidence artifact.
Cross-check the list against the BMA's published filing schedule for the entity's class and against last year's completed calendar.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the deadline derivation for each entry once, in writing.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed obligation inventory exists with a cite and deadline rule for every entry.

checklist.step: Load the calendar and configure alerts
actions: Create one tracker entry per obligation instance for the coming year, computing concrete due dates from each deadline rule and the entity's financial year-end.
Attach the owning role and a named individual to every entry, with the Regulatory Reporting Manager as backstop assignee.
Configure T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10/T-1 alerts on annual items and same-day alerts on event-driven windows (e.g. 14-day notifications).
Peer-check ten computed due dates against manual recomputation before publishing the calendar.
checklist.done: every obligation instance has a dated tracker entry, a named owner and firing alerts, with dates peer-checked.

checklist.step: Register event-driven triggers with the teams that see them first
actions: Brief the Corporate Secretary, HR and Finance on the events that start statutory clocks — auditor cessation, officer/controller changes, material transactions — and the exact day each window opens.
Agree a same-day notification route from each team into the filing tracker when a trigger event occurs.
Add a standing agenda item at the monthly compliance meeting to sweep for unreported trigger events.
Document the trigger map in the procedure.
checklist.done: every clock-starting event has a named spotting team and a same-day route into the tracker.

checklist.step: Track each filing to completion and capture proof of timeliness
actions: On each filing, attach the submission receipt (ERICA confirmation, courier record or acknowledged email) to the tracker entry and set status Filed with the actual date.
Compare actual date to due date; mark any late item as an exception immediately, never quietly closed.
Record the evidence-pack location link on the entry so the filing and its support are one click apart.
Run a weekly open-items report to the Regulatory Reporting Manager showing everything due in 30 days.
checklist.done: every calendar entry closes with a dated receipt, an evidence link, and lateness flagged as an exception.

checklist.step: Assemble a standard evidence pack behind every filing
actions: For each filing, collect the as-filed document, source extracts, reconciliations and tie-out working papers, approvals and the submission receipt into one folder named <entity>-<obligation>-<period>.
Check the pack against the evidence-pack standard checklist in the procedure before closing it.
Store the pack in the compliance evidence repository and mirror it to the Bermuda principal office share, since s.18 production happens there.
Apply the five-year retention label from the filing date.
checklist.done: each filed item has a complete, standard, retention-labelled pack mirrored to the principal office.

checklist.step: Keep the statutory records at the head office in Bermuda
actions: Maintain the index of statutory records the 1980 Regulations require to be kept, and where each physically or electronically resides.
Verify quarterly with the principal representative's office that the Bermuda share holds current mirrors of every indexed record, supporting the s.8/s.8B head-office substance.
Log and fix any record found only outside Bermuda or only with a third-party administrator.
Report the quarterly verification result to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the quarterly verification shows every indexed statutory record current and retrievable in Bermuda.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly retrieval fire-drill
actions: Pick two filed obligations at random each quarter and simulate a BMA s.18 production request against them.
Retrieve the full evidence pack from the repository and the Bermuda mirror within the 5-business-day internal standard, timing the retrieval.
Check pack completeness against the standard; any missing artifact is an exception with a named owner.
Record the drill result in the tracker.
checklist.done: two packs per quarter retrieve complete within 5 business days, or exceptions are raised.

checklist.step: Refresh the calendar on every regulatory change
actions: Monitor BMA notices, consultation papers and Insurance Act amendments monthly from the BMA website and counsel updates.
Assess each change for new, amended or retired obligations and deadline shifts, recording the assessment against the inventory.
Update the inventory and calendar entries within 10 business days of a confirmed change and re-run counsel confirmation on new deadline rules.
Announce material changes to all filing owners.
checklist.done: every confirmed regulatory change is reflected in the inventory and calendar within 10 business days.

checklist.step: Service actual BMA production requests
actions: Log any BMA information or production request the day it arrives, notify the principal representative and Head of Compliance, and set the response deadline the request states.
Assemble the response entirely from archived evidence packs; anything reconstructed after the fact must be labelled as such.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the response where any requested filing was late or amended.
Deliver by the BMA's stated channel and file the transmittal proof.
checklist.done: the request is logged, answered from archived evidence by the stated deadline, and the transmittal is filed.

checklist.step: Escalate at-risk deadlines before they are missed
actions: Flag any entry where the owner reports the deliverable will not be ready at T-10.
Escalate same-day to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the accountable executive with the options: accelerate, or apply to the BMA for an extension before the due date.
Where an extension is sought, file the BMA application and attach the grant or refusal to the calendar entry.
Record the decision and outcome on the entry.
checklist.done: no deadline passes unescalated; every at-risk item shows a decision and, where sought, the BMA extension outcome.

checklist.step: Report calendar health to governance
actions: Produce a monthly dashboard: items due in 60 days, completed on time %, open exceptions, retrieval-drill results.
Present it at the monthly compliance meeting and quarterly to the Head of Compliance and CFO.
Minute any accepted risk (e.g. a consciously deferred filing with BMA agreement) with its approver.
Archive each month's dashboard snapshot.
checklist.done: governance sees a monthly on-time and exception picture, and accepted risks carry a minuted approver.

checklist.step: Maintain owner continuity through people changes
actions: On any filing owner leaving or changing role, reassign every open calendar entry to a named successor within 5 business days.
Hand over the obligation inventory, evidence-pack standard and open items in a documented session.
Verify alert routing follows the reassignment in the tracker.
Note the handover on each affected entry.
checklist.done: no calendar entry is ever ownerless; handovers are documented and alerts follow the new owner.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to what was actually filed
actions: Quarterly, list every submission receipt held in the evidence repository and match each to a calendar entry.
Investigate receipts with no calendar entry (an untracked obligation was met ad hoc) and calendar entries with no receipt (a possible miss).
Add newly discovered obligations to the inventory with counsel confirmation.
Record the reconciliation result in the tracker.
checklist.done: receipts and calendar entries reconcile both ways each quarter, and discoveries update the inventory.

checklist.step: Log and remediate every exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue per late filing, calendar gap, failed drill or broken mirror with root cause and impact.
Assign an owner and remediation date; for late statutory filings, route to Regulatory Counsel for a BMA self-report assessment.
Track to closure and retest the fixed control at the next drill.
Summarise open exceptions on the monthly dashboard.
checklist.done: every exception carries cause, owner, date, any self-report decision, and a retest.

checklist.step: Re-approve the procedure annually
actions: Review the procedure, obligation inventory and evidence-pack standard once a year against the current Act, Regulations and BMA guidance.
Sign the re-approval and date it; record changes in the version history.
Confirm the annual inventory rebuild happened and its counsel confirmation is current.
File the approved version in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a dated annual re-approval exists with a current, counsel-confirmed inventory behind it.

testing.step: Independently rebuild the obligation inventory
actions: From the Insurance Act 1978, the 1980 Regulations and the entity's registration conditions, independently list the Bermuda obligations and deadline rules without reference to the team's inventory.
Compare to the maintained inventory; any obligation present in law but absent from the inventory is an exception regardless of whether it was met.
Check the counsel confirmation on deadline derivations is current.
testing.done: the independent rebuild matches the inventory, or gaps are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Build the population of obligations due in the trailing 12 months
actions: Export all calendar entries with due dates in the trailing 12 months, with status, owner, receipt and evidence link.
Reconcile the export against the independent inventory instantiated over the same period.
Resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: a reconciled population of due obligations exists with status and evidence links.

testing.step: Verify timeliness across the whole population
actions: For every population row, compare the receipt date to the recomputed statutory due date — full coverage, no sampling, since dates are cheap to check.
Sight the BMA extension grant for any item filed after the original date under an extension.
List every late or receiptless item as an exception.
testing.done: every due obligation is proven on time, extension-covered, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Sample evidence packs and test completeness
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 10 filed items (minimum, or 25% of the population if larger) and record the seed and selection date.
Retrieve each pack and check it against the evidence-pack standard: as-filed document, sources, reconciliations, approvals, receipt.
Time each retrieval against the 5-business-day standard.
Verify each pack also retrieves from the Bermuda principal office mirror.
testing.done: every sampled pack is complete, timely to retrieve, and present on the Bermuda mirror.

testing.step: Re-perform deadline computation on sampled entries
actions: For each sampled item, recompute the due date from the statutory rule (e.g. year-end + 4 months; event + 14 days; 31 March) and compare to the calendar entry.
Check the alert configuration actually fired by inspecting the tracker's alert log for the entry.
Flag any hand-keyed date that differs from the rule-derived date.
testing.done: sampled due dates re-derive from statute and alerts demonstrably fired.

testing.step: Test event-driven trigger capture
actions: Select trigger events from independent sources — board minutes, HR changes to officers, audit committee records — for the trailing period.
For each event that starts a statutory clock, confirm a tracker entry was opened the day the spotting team knew of it.
Any clock-starting event with no same-day entry is an exception even if the eventual filing was on time.
testing.done: independently sourced trigger events all map to same-day tracker entries.

testing.step: Test the head-office records requirement
actions: Pick five statutory records from the Records Manager's index and verify current versions retrieve from the Bermuda principal office share.
Inspect the last four quarterly verification reports for completeness and any unremediated gaps.
Check records held by third-party administrators are mirrored, not merely referenced.
testing.done: sampled statutory records retrieve in Bermuda and quarterly verifications show no open gaps.

testing.step: Verify the regulatory-change process kept the calendar current
actions: List BMA rule changes and Act amendments published in the trailing period from the BMA website.
For each, sight the documented impact assessment and, where obligations changed, the calendar update within 10 business days.
An unassessed published change is an exception.
testing.done: every published change in the period has an assessment and a timely calendar update where needed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the obligation, failure mode and statutory exposure under s.17/s.18.
Assign root cause, owner and remediation date; route late statutory filings to Regulatory Counsel for self-report assessment.
Carry open exceptions into the next semi-annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time and pack-completeness rates against the thresholds (zero missed statutory deadlines; all sampled packs complete) and state the conclusion.
Have the independent reviewer — who maintains neither the calendar nor any pack — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance and CFO and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C19.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to governance.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and the Head of Compliance; refreshed on any BMA class-structure or minimum-criteria change

Deadline reminders configured.value: Entry-gate checklist blocks launch until the certificate check is signed; tracker alerts on every open BMA application and notification window

checklist.step: Maintain the authoritative registration register
actions: Record for each Bermuda entity: registration class (1/2/3/3A/3B/4, C/D/E for long-term), certificate date, BMA-imposed conditions, approved business plan scope and any s.56 modifications.
Image the current certificate of registration and every BMA condition letter into the compliance evidence repository, linked from the register row.
Reconcile the register quarterly against the BMA's public register of insurers and log any discrepancy same-day.
Publish a read-only register view to Underwriting and Product leadership.
checklist.done: the register matches the BMA public register quarterly and every row links to an imaged certificate.

checklist.step: Define what the current certificate actually permits
actions: Read the certificate, the registered class definition in the Act and the BMA-approved business plan together, and write a plain-language scope statement: classes, lines, and any geographic or cession limits.
List the conditions attached to registration and translate each into an operational rule (e.g. no long-term business, cessions capped, pre-approval needed for X).
Publish the scope statement to the entry-gate checklist so non-lawyers apply it consistently.
Re-issue the statement whenever the certificate, conditions or business plan change.
checklist.done: a current counsel-issued scope statement exists and the entry-gate checklist references it.

checklist.step: Gate every new product, line or market behind a certificate check
actions: Require every new product, class, line-of-business or territory proposal to open an entry-gate case before pricing or distribution work commits launch dates.
Compare the proposal against the counsel scope statement and record COVERED, NOT COVERED, or CONDITIONS APPLY with the reasoning.
Block the launch milestone in the case tool for anything NOT COVERED until registration is varied or obtained.
Have the Chief Underwriting Officer's delegate acknowledge the gate outcome in writing.
checklist.done: every launch proposal carries a documented gate outcome acknowledged by underwriting leadership.

checklist.step: Prepare the s.4 application or variation when scope must grow
actions: Assemble the BMA application pack: proposed class, revised business plan, pro-forma financials showing the class minimum paid-up capital and solvency margin, and the Schedule 1 minimum-criteria evidence for controllers and officers.
Engage the BMA's Licensing team on a pre-submission call and log their steers in the application file.
Submit through the BMA's application channel and diarise follow-ups until grant.
On grant, image the new certificate, update the register and have counsel re-issue the scope statement.
checklist.done: the application is granted, the register and scope statement are updated, and the certificate is imaged.

checklist.step: Prove capital meets the class minimum before entry
actions: Confirm fully paid-up share capital meets the statutory minimum for the target class (e.g. USD 1m for Class 3A/3B; higher for Class 4/E) from the share register and audited equity note.
Confirm the projected MSM and ECR for the expanded scope from the BSCR pro-forma prepared with the Capital Model Actuary.
Where capital must be injected, evidence the paid-up injection (bank confirmation, board resolution) before the application is filed.
File the capital evidence in the application pack.
checklist.done: paid-up capital and projected solvency for the target class are evidenced before the BMA sees the application.

checklist.step: Wire the certificate scope into underwriting systems
actions: Translate the scope statement into underwriting platform reference data: permitted classes, lines and territories per legal entity.
Configure a hard block on binding any submission coded to an entity/class combination outside the register scope.
Test the block with a dummy out-of-scope submission and file the test evidence.
Re-run the configuration update within 5 business days of any certificate change.
checklist.done: the underwriting platform demonstrably blocks out-of-scope binds and reflects the current certificate.

checklist.step: Detect and notify material changes under s.30JA/30JB
actions: Maintain the material-change trigger list from s.30JA/30JB — e.g. change of business plan, mergers, acquisitions or disposals, new controllers — with the notification/no-objection route for each.
Brief Corporate Development and the Corporate Secretary so deals route to compliance before signing, not after.
File each notification with the BMA inside its statutory window and hold the transaction where prior no-objection is required.
Attach the BMA acknowledgement or non-objection to the register row.
checklist.done: every material change in the period shows a timely notification or non-objection on the register.

checklist.step: Keep the registration in good standing
actions: Track the annual BMA fee (due 31 March) and confirm payment against the registration each year from the C19 calendar.
Track any BMA condition with a recurring proof obligation and evidence compliance on schedule.
Sweep BMA correspondence monthly for anything touching registration status and log it.
Alert Regulatory Counsel immediately on any BMA letter mentioning s.41 (cancellation) or s.32 (directions).
checklist.done: fees and condition proofs are current and no registration-status correspondence sits unactioned.

checklist.step: Verify counterparty and fronting registrations where relied on
actions: Where a market entry relies on a Bermuda-registered affiliate, fronting carrier or reinsurer, check that party's registration and class on the BMA public register before the structure binds.
Record the check date and register extract in the treaty or entry file.
Recheck annually at renewal and on any adverse news about the counterparty.
Escalate lapsed or mismatched counterparty registrations to the Head of Reinsurance.
checklist.done: every relied-on Bermuda counterparty has a dated register check in the file, refreshed at renewal.

checklist.step: Sweep for business written outside the certificate
actions: Quarterly, extract all bound policies by legal entity, class, line and territory from the policy administration platform.
Compare each combination against the registration register scope; list any bind outside scope.
Investigate hits with Underwriting to separate miscoding from genuine out-of-scope writing.
Report genuine out-of-scope writing to the General Counsel the same day as a potential s.4 breach.
checklist.done: the quarterly sweep is complete and any genuine out-of-scope bind is escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Remediate out-of-scope writing under counsel direction
actions: Assess each confirmed out-of-scope bind: options include cancellation/novation, retroactive BMA engagement, or registration variation, with policyholder-protection duties considered first.
Decide and document the BMA disclosure approach — proactive disclosure is the default for a s.4 breach.
Direct the fix, assign owners and dates, and require underwriting-control changes so the same gap cannot recur.
Sign off closure of the exception once remediation and disclosure are complete.
checklist.done: every confirmed breach has a counsel-directed, documented remediation and disclosure decision, signed off.

checklist.step: Refresh minimum-criteria evidence for controllers and officers
actions: Keep the Schedule 1 minimum-criteria file current for each controller and officer counted in the registration: fitness and propriety declarations, and the s.30 notification history.
On any new controller or officer, run the item C24 screening and file the BMA notification within its window.
Review the file annually against the current org chart and shareholder register.
Log gaps as exceptions with owners.
checklist.done: the minimum-criteria file matches the current controllers and officers with no unnotified changes.

checklist.step: Train the front line on the entry gate
actions: Build a short module covering what the certificate permits, the entry-gate process and the consequence of unregistered business under the Act.
Assign it annually to Underwriting, Product and Distribution staff who can commit the company to new business.
Track completion to 100% within 30 days of assignment and chase non-completers weekly.
Refresh content whenever the scope statement changes.
checklist.done: assigned staff complete the module annually and content matches the current scope statement.

checklist.step: Archive the market-entry evidence per launch
actions: For each entry, file the gate case, scope comparison, certificate or variation grant, capital evidence and system-configuration proof under REG-057-C20 and the launch name.
Apply the retention label (life of registration plus five years).
Verify retrieval from the Bermuda principal office share.
Link the pack from the registration register row.
checklist.done: each launch has a complete, retention-labelled, Bermuda-retrievable evidence pack linked from the register.

checklist.step: Review the gate's effectiveness annually
actions: Review the year's gate cases, sweep results and exceptions with the Regulatory Affairs Manager and General Counsel.
Confirm the procedure, trigger list and scope statement reflect current law and BMA practice.
Sign the annual review and set improvement actions with owners.
File the signed review in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed annual effectiveness review exists with improvement actions owned and dated.

testing.step: Build the population of market entries and material changes
actions: From product launch records, board minutes, underwriting platform configuration changes and Corporate Development deal logs, list every new product, class, line, territory and material corporate change in the trailing 12 months.
Build the list from these independent sources first, then compare to the entry-gate case log — gate cases must not define the population.
Any launch or notifiable change absent from the gate log is an immediate exception.
testing.done: an independently sourced population is reconciled to the gate log with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Verify the register against the BMA public register
actions: Look up each Bermuda entity on the BMA's public register of insurers and compare class and status to the internal registration register.
Sight the imaged certificate for each entity and check conditions recorded internally match the BMA condition letters.
Confirm the quarterly reconciliation ran all four quarters.
testing.done: internal register, imaged certificates and the BMA public register agree for every entity.

testing.step: Re-perform the scope decision on every population entry
actions: For each launch, independently compare the product's class, line and territory to the certificate and counsel scope statement as they stood at launch date.
Reach your own COVERED / NOT COVERED conclusion before reading the gate case outcome.
Any divergence from the recorded gate outcome, or any launch pre-dating its certificate coverage, is an exception.
testing.done: every launch has an independent re-performed scope conclusion matching the gate record.

testing.step: Trace registrations and variations to BMA grants
actions: For each launch that needed new or varied registration, sight the BMA grant letter and check its date precedes the first bound policy.
Verify the capital evidence in the application pack shows paid-up capital at or above the class minimum at grant.
Confirm the register and scope statement were updated within 5 business days of grant.
testing.done: every scope expansion traces to a BMA grant dated before first business, with capital evidenced.

testing.step: Test the underwriting platform block
actions: Inspect the platform's permitted class/line/territory reference data against the current certificate scope.
Re-run the out-of-scope dummy submission test and confirm the hard block fires.
Check configuration change logs show updates within 5 business days of each certificate change in the period.
testing.done: the block fires on test and configuration history tracks certificate changes on time.

testing.step: Re-run the out-of-scope writing sweep independently
actions: Extract all policies bound in the period by entity, class, line and territory and compare to the register scope, without reference to the team's quarterly sweeps.
Compare hits to the team's sweep results; a hit the sweep missed is a control failure even if the bind was in scope after investigation.
For confirmed out-of-scope binds, verify same-day escalation to the General Counsel occurred.
testing.done: the independent sweep matches the team's results and confirmed breaches show same-day escalation.

testing.step: Test material-change notifications against statutory windows
actions: For each s.30JA/30JB-notifiable event in the population, sight the BMA notification or non-objection and compare its date to the statutory window from the event date.
For events needing prior no-objection, confirm the transaction did not complete before the BMA response.
An unnotified notifiable event is a fail regardless of outcome.

Confirm the dated register extract sits in the file for both points.

Route any s.4 breach to the General Counsel for the disclosure decision and record it on the issue.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception carries cause, owner, date and — for breaches — a documented disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report

Have the independent reviewer — uninvolved in any gate case or application — sign the workpaper.

testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the intermediary and producer register
actions: Record every broker, agent and producer authorised to solicit or place the company's business: legal name, jurisdiction, registration/licence type, verification date and expiry.
For Bermuda intermediaries, verify registration under s.10 of the Insurance Act on the BMA public register and attach the dated extract.
For US-resident producers placing US-sourced business, run the licence lookup in NIPR and attach the producer report showing active state licences and lines of authority.
Set the register status to AUTHORISED only when verification evidence is attached and current.
checklist.done: every register row carries a dated, attached verification and an explicit AUTHORISED status.

checklist.step: Gate first solicitation behind verification
actions: Configure the producer management system so submission intake and broker portal access require an AUTHORISED register status.
Require Underwriting to reject submissions from any intermediary not on the register and route the intermediary to onboarding instead.
Test the gate quarterly with a dummy unregistered intermediary code and file the evidence.
Report gate bypasses to the Producer Compliance Manager same-day.
checklist.done: no submission can enter from an unverified intermediary and the quarterly gate test passes.

checklist.step: Re-verify intermediaries annually and on adverse signals
actions: Run the annual re-verification cycle: refresh the BMA register extract for Bermuda intermediaries and the NIPR report for US producers before each row's expiry date.
Subscribe to BMA enforcement notices and state regulatory action feeds; on any adverse action, suspend the register status pending review.
Move lapsed or suspended intermediaries to BLOCKED and notify Underwriting and the Broker Relationship Manager the same day.
Log every status change with its evidence.
checklist.done: no register row is past its re-verification date and adverse actions trigger same-day blocking.

checklist.step: Maintain the exit-trigger watchlist
actions: List the events that can amount to ceasing to carry on insurance business — stopping new business in a class, mass non-renewal, portfolio sale, group restructure, solvency-driven wind-down.
Review board and executive committee minutes monthly for any of these signals and open a watchlist entry when one appears.
Brief Corporate Development and Underwriting leadership that no exit step is taken before Regulatory Counsel is engaged.
Report the watchlist at the monthly compliance meeting.
checklist.done: exit signals are swept monthly from minutes and every live signal has a watchlist entry.

checklist.step: Engage the BMA before any cessation decision is executed
actions: On a confirmed exit decision, notify the BMA in writing of the intention to cease carrying on insurance business (in whole or for the affected class) before any external step — citing s.41 and requesting the Authority's direction on cancellation terms.
Propose the run-off approach in the notification: natural expiry run-off, commutation programme, or transfer under s.25/s.27 with Schedule requirements.
Hold all cessation actions (mass non-renewals, transfer signings) until the BMA's response and any conditions are received.
File all correspondence with the principal representative copied.
checklist.done: the BMA is notified before any cessation step and the company holds until terms are agreed.

checklist.step: Build the run-off plan the BMA can accept
actions: Draft the run-off plan: liability projection to extinction from the Reserving Actuary, capital and MSM/ECR maintenance through run-off from the Capital Model Actuary, claims-handling arrangements, and reinsurance protections.
Confirm continued filing obligations (SFR/CSR through run-off) and governance (principal representative, approved auditor retained) are budgeted and owned.
Obtain board approval of the plan and submit it to the BMA with the s.41 dialogue.
Version-control the plan as BMA comments arrive.
checklist.done: a board-approved run-off plan with actuarial and capital support sits with the BMA.

checklist.step: Execute portfolio transfers only through the statutory scheme
actions: Where exit uses a transfer of business, follow s.25/s.27 and the Schedule: scheme documentation, independent actuary involvement where required, policyholder notice, and BMA (and where applicable court) approval before effectiveness.
Verify the transferee's registration covers the transferring business class before the scheme is lodged.
Diarise every scheme milestone in the filing tracker and hold completion until all approvals land.
File the sanctioned scheme and approvals in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: any transfer completes only after the statutory scheme and approvals, with the transferee's scope verified.

checklist.step: Manage policyholder communications during exit
actions: Draft non-renewal and run-off communications that meet the notice periods of each policy's governing law and any BMA conditions.
Sequence communications after BMA engagement so no policyholder learns of cessation before the regulator.
Stand up a policyholder query route (dedicated contact, FAQ) and log complaint volumes to the Complaints Manager.
Archive every communication template and send-log.
checklist.done: policyholder notices go out on lawful notice periods, after BMA engagement, with a working query route.

checklist.step: Notify officer and controller changes during exit under s.30
actions: Track resignations and appointments of directors, officers and controllers through the exit period — exits churn leadership — and file each s.30 notification within its statutory window.
Keep the principal representative and approved auditor appointments continuously filled through run-off; any cessation of either triggers its own 14-day notification.
Minute each change and cross-reference the C22 appointment log.
Reconcile the officer roster to BMA records quarterly during run-off.
checklist.done: all officer/controller changes through the exit are notified on time and statutory appointments never lapse.

checklist.step: Wind down distribution in step with the exit
actions: On the exit decision, set affected classes to CLOSED in the producer management system so intermediaries cannot submit new business in them.
Send termination or scope-reduction notices to affected intermediaries per their agreement terms, sequenced after BMA engagement.
Process trailing commissions and account settlements through the billing/commission platform with the Commission Analyst.
Keep servicing access open for in-force policies through run-off.
checklist.done: new-business access is closed for exited classes while in-force servicing continues, with settlements processed.

checklist.step: Maintain filings and capital through run-off until cancellation
actions: Continue SFR/CSR filings, fee payments and the s.8A declaration on the C19 calendar until the BMA cancels the registration — run-off does not suspend them.
Monitor capital against the MSM/ECR quarterly with the Capital Management Manager and report any deterioration to the BMA per the agreed plan.
Apply to the BMA for cancellation under s.41 only when liabilities are extinguished or transferred, attaching the final accounts.
File the BMA's cancellation confirmation as the closing record.
checklist.done: all obligations run to the cancellation date and the BMA's cancellation confirmation is on file.

checklist.step: Screen exiting-market producer terminations for reportability
actions: Where an intermediary relationship ends for cause (misconduct, misappropriation), assess regulatory reporting duties in each affected jurisdiction with Regulatory Counsel.
File any required for-cause termination reports within the jurisdiction's window and record the submission.
Preserve the investigation file for the retention period.
Cross-log the case in the C24 screening records.
checklist.done: every for-cause termination has a documented reportability assessment and any required report filed on time.

checklist.step: Keep evidence of the whole exit lifecycle
actions: File the exit decision minutes, BMA notifications and responses, run-off plan versions, scheme documents, policyholder notices and cancellation confirmation under REG-057-C21 and the exit name.
Apply a ten-year retention label from cessation.
Mirror the pack to the Bermuda principal office share.
Index by entity, class exited and year.
checklist.done: the exit pack is complete, retention-labelled and retrievable in Bermuda.

checklist.step: Run the annual no-exit attestation when no exit occurred
actions: Annually, review the watchlist, board minutes and underwriting class activity to confirm no cessation-in-substance occurred without the process.
Check for silent exits: classes with zero new business for 12+ months and no documented decision.
Obtain the Chief Underwriting Officer's written confirmation of class status intentions.
File the attestation with the year's evidence.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation confirms no unprocessed cessation, with silent-exit checks documented.

checklist.step: Review and re-approve the procedure
actions: Annually review verification volumes, gate-test results, watchlist activity and any exit conduct against the procedure.
Update for BMA guidance changes on run-off and intermediary supervision, and re-approve with the General Counsel.
Set improvement actions with owners and dates.
File the signed review.
checklist.done: a dated re-approval exists and improvement actions are owned.

testing.step: Build the placing-intermediary population from bound business
actions: Extract every intermediary code attached to business bound in the trailing 12 months from the policy administration platform.
Reconcile the code list to the producer register — the bound-business extract, not the register, defines who actually placed business.
Any placing code absent from the register is an immediate exception.
testing.done: the placing population is derived from bound business and reconciled to the register.

testing.step: Verify pre-solicitation verification for a sample
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 25 placing intermediaries plus all intermediaries first authorised in the period.
For each, sight the verification evidence (BMA register extract or NIPR report) and check its date precedes the intermediary's first submission date.
Re-perform the lookup today for five of them — on the BMA public register or in NIPR — and compare status.
Verification dated after first solicitation is a fail.
testing.done: every sampled intermediary shows verification pre-dating first solicitation, with re-lookups matching.

testing.step: Test the intake gate against unverified intermediaries
actions: Inspect the producer management system configuration requiring AUTHORISED status for submission intake and portal access.
Review the quarterly gate-test evidence for all four quarters.
Attempt a test submission under a BLOCKED code in a non-production environment and confirm rejection.
testing.done: the gate configuration, quarterly tests and the re-performed rejection all hold.

testing.step: Test re-verification currency across the register
actions: Export the full register and compute days since last verification for every AUTHORISED row.
Flag any row beyond its annual re-verification date as an exception.
Trace three adverse-action events from BMA/state feeds in the period to same-day status suspensions.
testing.done: no AUTHORISED row is over-age and sampled adverse actions triggered same-day suspension.

testing.step: Build the population of exit events
actions: From board and executive minutes, Corporate Development logs and underwriting class-activity data, list every cessation decision, portfolio transfer and class with new business stopped in the period.
Include silent candidates: classes with zero new business for 12+ months.
Compare to the compliance watchlist; an exit signal the watchlist missed is a control exception.
testing.done: an independently sourced exit-event population exists, reconciled to the watchlist.

testing.step: Verify BMA engagement preceded every cessation step
actions: For each exit event, sight the s.41 notification to the BMA and compare its date to the first external cessation step (mass non-renewal issue date, transfer signing, intermediary terminations).
Read the BMA's response and confirm conditions were met before actions proceeded.
Any external step pre-dating BMA notification is a fail.
testing.done: every exit shows BMA notification before the first external step, with conditions honoured.

testing.step: Test transfer schemes against s.25/s.27 requirements
actions: For any portfolio transfer, verify the scheme file contains the Schedule-required elements: scheme document, actuarial input, policyholder notices and the BMA/court approvals.
Check approval dates precede the transfer effective date.
Verify the transferee's BMA registration covered the transferred class at effectiveness via the public register.
testing.done: transfers completed only after full statutory approvals with the transferee's scope confirmed.

testing.step: Verify run-off obligations continued
actions: For entities in run-off during the period, confirm SFR/CSR filings, fee payments and s.8A declarations continued on schedule via the C19 calendar receipts.
Confirm the principal representative and approved auditor appointments remained filled throughout.
Sight quarterly capital monitoring against MSM/ECR and any agreed BMA reporting.
testing.done: run-off entities show unbroken filings, appointments and capital monitoring.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the intermediary or exit event, the requirement breached (s.10 verification, s.41 sequence, s.25/s.27 scheme) and impact.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Route sequence breaches to the General Counsel for a BMA disclosure decision, recorded on the issue.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner, date and any disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Conclude against the thresholds (no unverified placement, no cessation step before BMA engagement) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — uninvolved in verification and exit decisions — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance and General Counsel and file the workpaper under REG-057-C21.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
