checklist.step: Maintain the statutory appointment register
actions: List every statutory post per Bermuda entity — approved auditor, principal representative, appointed/loss reserve actuary, and directors/officers within s.30 scope — with incumbent, appointment date, BMA approval reference and status.
Link each row to the board resolution and the BMA approval or acknowledgement letter in the evidence repository.
Review the register monthly against HR records and board minutes to catch unrecorded changes.
Publish the register to the General Counsel and Head of Compliance monthly.
checklist.done: the register shows a current, evidenced incumbent for every statutory post with no unrecorded changes at month-end.

checklist.step: Open a tracked case the day any appointment event occurs
actions: On learning of a resignation, removal, death or incapacity of a statutory appointee, open a tracker case the same day recording the event date — the statutory clock runs from the event, not from the paperwork.
Compute the day-14 notification deadline and set day-3/day-7/day-12 alerts.
Attach the resignation letter or removal resolution as the event evidence.
Notify Regulatory Counsel and the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: every appointment event has a same-day case with the 14-day deadline computed from the event date.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of auditor cessation within 14 days
actions: Draft the s.16A notification stating the auditor's cessation, the effective date and the reason, and attach the outgoing firm's statement of circumstances.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording where the cessation involves a disagreement or independence issue.
Dispatch to the BMA within 14 days of the event by the Authority's accepted channel and keep the dated dispatch proof.
Record the notification date on the register row and close the alert.
checklist.done: the cleared notification with statement of circumstances is dispatched inside day 14, with proof retained.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of principal representative changes within 14 days
actions: On the principal representative ceasing to act, send the s.8 notification to the BMA within 14 days stating the cessation date and the interim arrangement.
Where the representative resigns, obtain their statutory notice and reason and file it with the notification.
Confirm the principal office address in Bermuda remains valid through the change — s.5A/s.8(1) requires it — and notify any office move separately.
Record dispatch proof on the register.
checklist.done: principal representative cessation and any office change are notified inside the window with proofs filed.

checklist.step: Secure BMA approval before a successor acts
actions: For posts requiring BMA approval (approved auditor; principal representative and actuary where the class rules require), file the approval application with the candidate's qualifications before the appointment takes effect.
Instruct the candidate in writing not to sign, certify or represent the company in the statutory role until approval lands.
Chase the BMA at 10 business days if no response and log the follow-up.
On approval, date the register row from the approval, not from the board resolution.
checklist.done: no successor performs the statutory role before the BMA approval date recorded on the register.

checklist.step: Bridge vacancies so no statutory post lapses
actions: Where a replacement cannot be approved before the incumbent's cessation, agree an interim arrangement with the BMA in writing (e.g. extended notice period, interim appointee).
Document the bridge on the tracker case with the BMA's written acceptance.
Escalate to the CEO and board chair any vacancy risk in the approved auditor or principal representative post.
Close the case only when the permanent successor's approval is on the register.
checklist.done: any vacancy period is covered by a BMA-accepted bridge and closed by an approved successor.

checklist.step: Process board resolutions and officer notifications under s.30
actions: Minute every statutory appointment and termination through the board portal with the effective date explicit in the resolution.
File the s.30 notification of officer/controller changes with the BMA within its statutory window, attaching the new officer's particulars.
Cross-check that C24 fit-and-proper screening completed before the appointment resolution was tabled.
Update the register and the entity's public filings where required.
checklist.done: every change is minuted, screened, notified under s.30 on time, and reflected on the register.

checklist.step: Coordinate the appointed actuary transition
actions: On an actuary change, confirm the successor meets the BMA's qualification requirements for the entity's class and file any required approval before opinion work starts.
Run a documented handover: reserve basis, open BMA queries, prior opinion caveats, and model access.
Notify the BMA of the outgoing actuary's cessation within the statutory window with reasons.
Record both events on the register with evidence.
checklist.done: the actuary transition shows approval before opinion work, a documented handover, and timely notifications.

checklist.step: File the annual Declaration of Compliance on schedule
actions: Confirm with the C17 owner that the s.8A Declaration of Compliance is signed by the required signatories and filed with the SFR each year.
Verify the signatories held valid appointments on the register at signing date.
Record the declaration filing date on the appointment register year-record.
Escalate any signatory-eligibility doubt to Regulatory Counsel before signing.
checklist.done: the annual declaration is signed by register-verified signatories and filed with the SFR.

checklist.step: Keep dispatch-channel details current with the BMA
actions: Confirm annually the BMA's accepted channels and addressees for appointment notifications from the BMA website and recent correspondence.
Update the notification templates and the procedure with any change.
Test the e-submission route with a non-substantive query if unused for 12 months.
Record the annual confirmation in the tracker.
checklist.done: notification templates target the BMA's current channel, confirmed within the last year.

checklist.step: Train secretariat cover staff on the windows
actions: Document the same-day-case and 14-day-notification drill in a one-page runbook.
Train the Executive Assistant and Legal Secretary who cover secretariat absences, with a walkthrough of a past case.
Test cover annually by running a tabletop event during a planned absence.
Log training completion.
checklist.done: trained cover exists and the annual tabletop shows the window is met without the primary owner.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to external records quarterly
actions: Quarterly, reconcile the appointment register to the Registrar of Companies filings, the audit engagement letter, and the BMA's records where visible.
Investigate any mismatch (e.g. an officer filed externally but absent from the register) same-week.
Report reconciliation results to the Corporate Secretary with exceptions logged.
File the reconciliation evidence.
checklist.done: quarterly reconciliations complete with all mismatches investigated and logged.

checklist.step: Handle BMA queries and objections on appointments
actions: Log any BMA query or objection on an appointment in the tracker with its response date.
Respond from the register evidence and screening file; where the BMA objects to a candidate, pause the appointment and brief the board.
Record the resolution (approval, withdrawal, substitution) on the case.
Attach all correspondence to the register row.
checklist.done: every BMA appointment query is answered on time and objections pause the appointment until resolved.

checklist.step: Archive the appointment evidence per event
actions: File per event: the resolution, approval letter, notification with dispatch proof, and any bridge correspondence under REG-057-C22 and the event date.
Apply the five-year retention label and mirror to the Bermuda principal office share.
Link the pack from the register row.
Verify retrieval in the quarterly records check.
checklist.done: each event's pack is complete, labelled, mirrored and linked from the register.

checklist.step: Review the year's events and re-approve the procedure
actions: Annually review all appointment events, notification timings and any bridges against the procedure.
Update the procedure for Insurance Act amendments and BMA practice changes, and sign the re-approval.
Set owners for any weakness (e.g. events reaching the secretariat late).
File the signed review.
checklist.done: a dated re-approval exists and weaknesses carry named owners.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment events from independent sources

Build the list before opening the appointment register, then reconcile — events the register missed are exceptions in themselves.
Cover every Bermuda entity in the group.
testing.done: an independently sourced event population is reconciled to the register with misses flagged.

testing.step: Recompute every notification window
actions: For each cessation event, establish the true event date from the primary evidence (resignation letter date of effect, removal resolution), not the case-open date.
Recompute event date plus 14 days and compare to the dated dispatch proof of the BMA notification.
Any dispatch after day 14, or any notification evidenced only by an undated copy, is a fail.
testing.done: every notification is proven dispatched within 14 days of the true event date.

testing.step: Verify approvals preceded successor activity
actions: For each new approved auditor, principal representative or actuary, sight the BMA approval letter and its date.
Search for the successor's first act in the role — first signed opinion, first BMA correspondence as representative, first certification — and compare dates.
Any act pre-dating approval is a fail.
testing.done: no successor's first act in a statutory role pre-dates the BMA approval.

testing.step: Test vacancy coverage
actions: For each event, compute the gap between the incumbent's cessation and the successor's approved start.
Where a gap exists, sight the BMA's written acceptance of the bridge arrangement.
An uncovered gap in the auditor or principal representative post is a reportable finding.
testing.done: every vacancy period is either zero or covered by BMA-accepted bridging.

testing.step: Test s.30 officer notifications
actions: For officer and controller changes in the population, sight the s.30 notification and check timing against the statutory window.
Verify C24 screening evidence pre-dates each appointment resolution.
Check the new officer's particulars in the notification match the board resolution.
testing.done: all officer changes show timely s.30 notifications with prior screening.

testing.step: Verify register accuracy and reconciliations
actions: Sample five register rows and trace each field (incumbent, dates, approval reference) to source documents.
Inspect the four quarterly reconciliations to Registrar and engagement records for completion and cleared mismatches.
Check every register row links to an evidence pack that opens.
testing.done: sampled rows trace cleanly, reconciliations ran quarterly, and all evidence links resolve.

testing.step: Verify the annual declaration linkage
actions: Sight the year's s.8A Declaration of Compliance and confirm the signatories held valid register appointments on the signing date.
Confirm the declaration was filed with the SFR per the C17 evidence.
Flag any signatory whose appointment evidence post-dates signing.
testing.done: the declaration's signatories are register-verified as validly appointed at signing.

testing.step: Test the cover arrangement
actions: Sight the runbook and the training records for secretariat cover staff.
Review the annual tabletop result and check any event handled by cover staff in the period met the window.
Flag single-person dependency if no tabletop ran.
testing.done: cover is trained, tabletop-tested, and cover-handled events met the statutory window.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the event, requirement breached (14-day window, prior approval, s.30) and impact.
Assign root cause (event reached secretariat late, clock started from wrong date) with owner and date.
Route late notifications to the General Counsel for the BMA disclosure decision.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner, date and any disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Conclude against the thresholds (no late notification, no pre-approval activity, no uncovered vacancy) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who processed no event in the period — sign the workpaper.
Report to the General Counsel and Audit Committee and file the workpaper under REG-057-C22.

checklist.step: Build the consolidated renewal log for the cycle
actions: Create one log entry per renewable item: the BMA annual fee (due 31 March), the s.8A declaration (with the SFR), each Bermuda intermediary's s.10 registration renewal, and each US producer's licence expiry per state.
For US producers, pull licence class, expiry date and CE due date per state from NIPR producer reports rather than keying dates by hand.
Attach the fee invoice or renewal notice where one exists and name a responsible owner per entry.
Peer-check ten entries against source documents before publishing the log.
checklist.done: every renewable item has a dated, owned, source-backed log entry for the cycle.

checklist.step: Configure the alert ladder on every entry
actions: Set 90/60/30/7-day alerts before each expiry, routed to the entry owner with the coordinator copied.
Configure the day-0 rule: any entry not marked complete on its due date auto-flags the intermediary or producer to BLOCKED in the register feeding the C21 intake gate.
Test the alert chain on a dummy entry each cycle and file the evidence.
Document alert routing in the procedure.
checklist.done: alerts demonstrably fire on schedule and day-0 lapses auto-block solicitation.

checklist.step: Pay the BMA annual fee before 31 March
actions: Confirm the fee amount for each entity's registration class from the BMA's current fee schedule on bma.bm.
Raise the payment request to Treasury by 1 March with the entity, class and amount, and track approval through the finance workflow.
Confirm settlement with the Treasury Analyst and obtain the payment confirmation referencing the entity.
Attach the confirmation to the renewal-log entry and mark complete before 31 March.
checklist.done: the correct class fee for every entity is confirmed paid with evidence before 31 March.

checklist.step: Track the annual declaration through the SFR filing
actions: Link the s.8A Declaration of Compliance log entry to the C17/C22 owners and their filing calendar entry.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that the signed declaration went into the ERICA package, and record the filing date on the log.
Mark complete only on sight of the ERICA receipt.
Escalate at T-30 if the declaration draft is not yet circulating.
checklist.done: the declaration entry closes against the ERICA receipt, never on verbal confirmation.

checklist.step: Renew Bermuda intermediary registrations on time
actions: At the 60-day alert, contact each Bermuda intermediary's compliance contact and request their renewal confirmation or updated s.10 registration evidence.
Verify the renewed status on the BMA public register once the intermediary confirms, and attach the dated extract.
Where an intermediary will not renew, hand the relationship to the Broker Relationship Manager for wind-down and set the register to BLOCKED at expiry.
Record completion on the log.
checklist.done: every Bermuda intermediary entry closes with a post-renewal BMA register extract or a managed wind-down.

checklist.step: Process US producer licence renewals through NIPR
actions: At the 60-day alert, run the producer's licence status in NIPR and confirm whether the producer or their agency handles the renewal transaction.
For company-managed renewals, submit the renewal in NIPR for the expiring state licence, pay the state fee, and download the transaction confirmation.
Re-run the NIPR report after the state processes the renewal and attach the report showing the new expiry date.
Mark the log entry complete only when the post-renewal report is attached.
checklist.done: each US producer entry closes with a NIPR report showing an active licence and new expiry.

checklist.step: Track CE completion ahead of the licence renewal
actions: For each state that conditions renewal on continuing education, record the CE hours required and the completion deadline on the producer's log entry.
At the 90-day alert, request the producer's CE transcript or check compliance status via the state's CE administrator, and chase shortfalls monthly.
Flag producers with unmet CE at 30 days to the Producer Compliance Manager — an unmet CE requirement blocks the renewal from processing.
File the completion evidence with the entry.
checklist.done: CE status is evidenced ahead of every conditioned renewal and shortfalls are escalated at day 30.

checklist.step: Stop solicitation the day a licence lapses
actions: On any day-0 auto-block, confirm the producer management system shows BLOCKED and that portal/submission access is cut, per the C21 gate.
Notify the producer, their agency and the assigned underwriters the same day that no solicitation or binding may occur.
Quarantine any in-flight submissions from the lapsed producer pending reinstatement review.
Log the lapse as an exception with the discovery route.
checklist.done: lapses cut access same-day, stakeholders are told, and in-flight business is quarantined.

checklist.step: Handle reinstatements correctly
actions: For a lapsed US licence, verify the state's reinstatement rules (late-renewal window, penalty fee, re-examination threshold) and process reinstatement via NIPR where eligible.
Review whether any business was solicited or bound during the lapse window by matching submission dates against the lapse period.
Where lapse-period business is found, refer it to Regulatory Counsel for the state-notification decision and document the outcome.
Unblock only on an active post-reinstatement NIPR report.
checklist.done: reinstatements are evidence-based, lapse-period business is investigated, and unblocking requires a clean report.

checklist.step: Sweep monthly for silent expiries
actions: Monthly, batch-run NIPR reports for all active US producers and diff licence statuses against the renewal log.
Check the BMA public register monthly for any intermediary whose registration disappeared outside its expected cycle.
Open a log entry and investigation for any status change the alerts did not predict.
Report sweep results to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: monthly sweeps reconcile external status to the log and unpredicted changes are investigated.

checklist.step: Keep the per-jurisdiction deadline table current
actions: Maintain the reference table of renewal rules per jurisdiction: renewal cadence, CE hours, late windows and fee amounts, each with its source citation.
Review state bulletin feeds and the BMA fee schedule annually and on change notices, updating the table within 10 business days.
Version the table so the rule in force at any past renewal can be evidenced.
Publish updates to the coordinator.
checklist.done: the deadline table is current, cited, versioned, and updated within 10 business days of changes.

checklist.step: Report renewal-cycle health monthly
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard: entries due in 90 days, completed on time %, open lapses, CE shortfalls and Bermuda good-standing status.
Review it with the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution monthly.
Minute decisions on chronic late renewers (retrain, restrict or terminate the relationship).
Archive each snapshot.
checklist.done: governance sees monthly renewal health and chronic offenders get minuted decisions.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle's evidence
actions: File the cycle's renewal log export, fee confirmations, NIPR receipts, CE certificates and lapse investigations under REG-057-C23 and the cycle year.
Apply the five-year retention label.
Verify Bermuda-item evidence also mirrors to the principal office share.
Index by producer, jurisdiction and cycle.
checklist.done: the cycle's evidence set is archived, labelled and indexed.

checklist.step: Onboard new producers straight into the log
actions: On every new intermediary or producer authorisation from the C21 process, create renewal-log entries for all their expiry dates at onboarding, not at the first cycle build.
Verify the initial licence evidence carries an expiry date and load it with the alert ladder.
Cross-check quarterly that every AUTHORISED register row has at least one live renewal entry.
Fix orphans same-week.
checklist.done: no authorised producer exists without live renewal entries, verified quarterly.

checklist.step: Review and re-approve the procedure annually
actions: Review the cycle's on-time rate, lapse count and root causes with the Producer Compliance Manager.
Update the procedure for rule-table changes and process fixes, and sign the re-approval.
Set improvement actions with owners and dates.
File the signed review.
checklist.done: a dated re-approval exists with improvement actions owned.

testing.step: Build the population of renewable items independently
actions: From the C21 producer register (all AUTHORISED rows), the entity list and the BMA fee schedule, independently derive every item that required renewal in the trailing 12 months.
Reconcile to the renewal log — an item renewable in fact but absent from the log is an exception even if it renewed.
Record population size and sources in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently derived renewable population reconciles to the log with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Verify timeliness across the full population
actions: For every log entry, compare the completion evidence date to the due date — full coverage, since dates are cheap to check.
Confirm the BMA fee confirmation pre-dates 31 March and the declaration entry closed on an ERICA receipt.
List every late or evidence-free completion as an exception.
testing.done: every entry is proven timely and evidenced, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Re-verify licence status in the source systems
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 20 producer entries and re-run each producer's current status in NIPR (or the BMA public register for Bermuda intermediaries).
Compare the live expiry date to the log's recorded expiry; a mismatch means the log drifted from source.
Verify the attached post-renewal report genuinely shows the claimed new expiry.
testing.done: sampled log entries match live source-system status and attached evidence is genuine.

testing.step: Re-perform CE compliance checks on the sample
actions: For sampled producers in CE-conditioned states, sight the CE transcript or completion certificate against the state's required hours from the versioned rule table.
Recompute hours against the requirement in force at the renewal date.
Flag any renewal processed despite a CE shortfall for root-cause review.
testing.done: sampled CE evidence satisfies the hours in force at each renewal date.

testing.step: Test lapse handling end to end
actions: List every lapse in the period from the exception log and the monthly sweep results.
For each, verify the day-0 BLOCKED flag, the same-day notifications and the submission quarantine timestamps.
Match submission and bind dates against each lapse window to independently confirm no business was solicited or bound while lapsed.
Verify unblocking evidence is a post-reinstatement report, not an email assertion.
testing.done: every lapse shows same-day blocking, no lapse-window business, and evidence-based reinstatement.

testing.step: Test the alert ladder actually fired
actions: For ten sampled entries, inspect the system's alert log for the 90/60/30/7-day alert firings and their recipients.
Verify the dummy-entry alert test ran in the cycle and its evidence is filed.
An entry whose alerts silently failed is a control exception even if renewed on time.
testing.done: sampled alert histories show the ladder fired to the right owners.

testing.step: Verify the monthly sweeps ran and caught drift
actions: Sight the twelve monthly NIPR batch sweeps and BMA register checks and their diff results.
Trace two sweep-detected status changes to opened investigations.
A month with no sweep evidence is an exception.
testing.done: twelve monthly sweeps are evidenced with detected changes investigated.

testing.step: Verify the rule table's accuracy
actions: Sample five jurisdictions from the deadline table and re-verify cadence, CE hours and fee against the current state or BMA source.
Check the version history shows updates within 10 business days of known changes in the period.
A stale rule that drove a wrong deadline is a root-cause finding, not just a data error.
testing.done: sampled rules match current sources and the version history shows timely updates.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the item, jurisdiction, failure mode and impact.
Assign root cause (alert failure, stale rule, producer non-response) with a named owner and date.
Route any solicitation-while-lapsed finding to Regulatory Counsel for the state/BMA notification decision.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception carries cause, owner, date and any notification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Conclude against the thresholds (fee by 31 March, zero solicitation-while-lapsed, full log coverage) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who maintains no log entry — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance and file the workpaper under REG-057-C23.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Tier every role by screening risk
actions: Classify each job family into tiers: Tier 1 officers/controllers within Schedule 1 scope, Tier 2 positions of trust (claims payment, treasury, underwriting authority, US-facing producers), Tier 3 all other staff.

Define the check set per tier — identity, criminal record, regulatory-action search, sanctions, credit where lawfully permitted, and the 1033 felony question for any role touching US insurance business.
Review the tier map with the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel and publish it into the recruiting workflow.
Re-tier on any role change that adds authority.
checklist.done: every job family carries a published tier and check set, legally reviewed.

checklist.step: Open a screening case at offer stage, before any start date
actions: On offer acceptance, open the screening case from the requisition, recording role, tier, work location and whether the role touches US insurance business.
Issue the candidate the consent forms: background-check authorisation, the fit-and-proper declaration for Tier 1, and the felony-conviction disclosure question for US-facing roles.
Set the provisional start date in the HRIS only as PENDING SCREENING.
Hand the case to the screening analyst with the signed consents.
checklist.done: every accepted offer has an open case with signed consents and a start date gated on clearance.

checklist.step: Run the background checks for the tier
actions: Run identity verification, criminal-record checks in each jurisdiction of residence for the look-back period, and the regulatory-action search (BMA enforcement notices, state insurance department actions, FINRA/SEC where relevant) in LexisNexis Risk.
Screen the candidate against sanctions lists via the sanctions screening system and record the run reference.
For US-facing roles, review the felony disclosure answer against the criminal-record result — any breach-of-trust or dishonesty felony triggers the 1033 branch.
Attach every report to the case with run dates.
checklist.done: all tier-required checks are run, attached and dated on the case.

checklist.step: Adjudicate findings against the published standard
actions: Assess each finding against the adjudication matrix: relevance to the role, recency, severity and pattern — never ad-hoc judgement.
Record the decision (CLEARED, CLEARED WITH CONDITIONS, DECLINED) with written reasoning on the case.
Route Tier 1 adverse findings to the General Counsel and any 1033 trigger to Regulatory Counsel before deciding.
Give the candidate the adverse-action process required by applicable law before a DECLINED is finalised.
checklist.done: every finding shows a matrix-based, documented decision with the required escalations and candidate process.

checklist.step: Handle 1033 prohibited-person cases explicitly
actions: Where a candidate or producer has a felony conviction involving dishonesty or breach of trust and the role touches US insurance business, treat them as prohibited under 18 U.S.C. §1033(e) absent written consent.

Determine the consent authority — the insurance commissioner of the relevant state — and prepare the 1033 consent (waiver) application with the conviction records and rehabilitation evidence if the company wishes to proceed.
Bar any start or solicitation until the written consent is granted and filed on the case; otherwise close the case DECLINED.
Log the decision in the tracker with the statutory basis.
checklist.done: no prohibited person acts in US business without a granted, filed written consent.

checklist.step: Complete fit-and-proper packs for officers and controllers
actions: For Tier 1 appointments, assemble the Schedule 1 minimum-criteria pack: the signed fit-and-proper declaration, CV, qualification evidence, regulatory history and the screening results.
Deliver the pack to the Corporate Secretary so the s.30 notification (or s.30D no-objection for shareholder controllers) can be filed within its window per C22.
Confirm the appointment resolution is not tabled before the pack is complete.
File the pack in the appointment evidence set.
checklist.done: every officer/controller appointment carries a complete minimum-criteria pack feeding the C22 notification.

checklist.step: Enforce the start-date gate in the HRIS
actions: Keep the HRIS business process configured so onboarding tasks, system access requests and payroll setup cannot trigger while the screening case is not CLEARED.
On CLEARED, convert the provisional start date to confirmed and release onboarding.
On DECLINED, retract the offer through the documented adverse-action route with Employment Counsel.
Test the gate quarterly with a dummy candidate record and file the evidence.
checklist.done: the HRIS demonstrably blocks starts without clearance and the quarterly gate test passes.

checklist.step: Screen producers through the same gate at authorisation
actions: Require a completed screening case (background, regulatory-action, sanctions, 1033 question) before any producer or intermediary reaches AUTHORISED in the C21 register.
For US producers, corroborate the regulatory-action search with the NIPR producer report's licence status and any state actions.
Record the screening case reference on the producer register row.
Re-screen on adverse news and at least every three years for active producers.
checklist.done: no producer is AUTHORISED without a linked cleared screening case, refreshed on the cycle.

checklist.step: Catch internal moves into positions of trust
actions: Configure the HRIS transfer workflow to flag any move into a Tier 1 or Tier 2 role and open a screening-delta case.
Run only the incremental checks the new tier requires beyond the person's last screening.
Hold the transfer effective date until the delta case clears.
Record the case on the employee record.
checklist.done: tiered internal moves generate delta screenings that clear before the transfer takes effect.

checklist.step: Run ongoing integrity monitoring for in-post Tier 1 staff
actions: Annually re-run regulatory-action and sanctions checks for officers, controllers and Tier 1 staff.
Require annual re-attestation of the fit-and-proper declaration, including new convictions or regulatory actions.
Route any new adverse finding to the adjudication process and, for officers, to the Corporate Secretary for BMA notification assessment.
Log completion per person.
checklist.done: every Tier 1 incumbent has a current-year re-check and re-attestation, with findings adjudicated.

checklist.step: Protect screening data
actions: Restrict screening-case access to named Compliance and HR staff, enforced through the case system's access controls.
Set retention at employment plus five years and purge on schedule, with purge logs kept.
Confirm cross-border transfers of screening data (Bermuda/US/other) follow the privacy framework, documented per transfer route.
Review access lists semi-annually.
checklist.done: screening data is access-restricted, retention-scheduled, and transfer-compliant with semi-annual access reviews.

checklist.step: Handle screening bypasses as incidents
actions: On discovering any person who started or solicited before clearance, open an incident: run the missed checks immediately and suspend authority pending results.
Where results are adverse, apply the adjudication outcome up to termination and assess regulator notification with the General Counsel.
Root-cause the bypass (gate misconfiguration, manual override) and fix the control.
Sign off closure with the control fix evidenced.
checklist.done: every bypass is remediated with immediate checks, a control fix and a signed closure.

checklist.step: Report screening metrics to governance
actions: Publish monthly: cases opened/cleared, ageing beyond 10 business days, adverse findings by tier, bypass incidents and 1033 cases.
Review with the Chief HR Officer and Head of Compliance monthly.
Escalate chronic ageing to resourcing decisions.
Archive snapshots.
checklist.done: monthly metrics reach governance and ageing drives resourcing decisions.

checklist.step: Archive the screening evidence per case
actions: File per case: consents, reports, adjudication notes, 1033 evidence and the clearance record under REG-057-C24 by case reference.
Apply the retention label and the restricted-access marking.
Verify the case links from the HRIS record and, for producers, from the register row.
Confirm retrievability in the quarterly records check.
checklist.done: every case is archived, restricted, linked and retrievable by reference.

checklist.step: Review and re-approve the procedure annually
actions: Review tier map accuracy, adjudication consistency and bypass incidents annually with the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel.
Update for legal changes (state 1033 consent practice, Bermuda minimum-criteria guidance, privacy law) and sign the re-approval.
Set improvement actions with owners and dates.
File the signed review.
checklist.done: a dated, legally reviewed re-approval exists with owned improvement actions.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope starts and appointments
actions: Extract all hires and internal transfers into Tier 1/2 roles in the trailing 12 months from the HRIS, and all newly AUTHORISED producers from the C21 register.
Add officer/controller appointments from the C22 register and board minutes.
Reconcile the three sources; a person appearing in any source without a screening case is an immediate exception.
testing.done: a reconciled population of starts, moves, appointments and producers exists with caseless entries flagged.

testing.step: Test the gate across the full population
actions: For every population row, compare the screening case CLEARED date to the actual start date, transfer effective date, appointment resolution date or AUTHORISED date.
Full coverage, no sampling — the comparison is mechanical.
Any start preceding clearance is a fail; list each with the days of exposure.
testing.done: every start is proven to post-date clearance, or is listed as a fail with exposure quantified.

testing.step: Re-perform screening on a sample of cases
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 20 cases stratified across tiers, plus every case with an adverse finding.
Check each case holds all tier-required reports with run dates before clearance.
Re-run the regulatory-action and sanctions searches for five sampled subjects and compare to the filed results.
Missing tier-required checks in a CLEARED case is a fail.
testing.done: sampled cases hold complete, pre-clearance check sets and re-runs corroborate the filed results.

testing.step: Re-perform adjudication on adverse-finding cases
actions: For every adverse-finding case, re-apply the adjudication matrix to the filed evidence without reading the recorded decision first.
Compare conclusions; a divergence or an undocumented deviation from the matrix is an exception.
Verify the required escalations (General Counsel for Tier 1, Regulatory Counsel for 1033) are evidenced.
testing.done: every adverse decision re-derives from the matrix with escalations evidenced.

testing.step: Test 1033 handling end to end
actions: Identify every case where the felony disclosure or criminal check triggered the 1033 branch.
For proceeded cases, sight the state commissioner's written consent and check its date precedes any US-business activity by the person.
For declined cases, confirm the person never appeared in US-facing systems or producer registers.
Cross-check the criminal-record results of US-facing CLEARED cases for any breach-of-trust felony the branch missed.
testing.done: every 1033 trigger shows consent-before-activity or a clean decline, and no missed trigger exists in the sample.

testing.step: Verify officer packs fed the BMA notifications
actions: For each officer/controller appointment, sight the Schedule 1 minimum-criteria pack and check its completion date precedes the appointment resolution.
Trace the pack to the C22 s.30/s.30D notification and its timing.
An appointment resolved before its pack completed is an exception.
testing.done: every appointment shows pack-before-resolution and a traced, timely notification.

testing.step: Test the HRIS gate configuration and overrides
actions: Inspect the business-process configuration blocking onboarding without CLEARED status and review the quarterly dummy-candidate test evidence.
Pull the override/exception log for the period and verify each override carries documented Head of Compliance approval.
An unapproved override is a fail even if the person later cleared.
testing.done: the gate configuration holds, quarterly tests ran, and every override is approved and documented.

testing.step: Test ongoing monitoring and re-attestations
actions: For all current Tier 1 incumbents, verify a current-year re-check and signed re-attestation exist.
Trace any new adverse finding in the period to an adjudication and, for officers, a BMA-notification assessment.
Verify producer re-screens occurred within the three-year cycle for a sample of five.
testing.done: Tier 1 monitoring is current, findings were adjudicated, and producer re-screens meet the cycle.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the case reference (no personal detail), failure mode and exposure.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Route any prohibited-person or bypass finding to the General Counsel for the regulator-notification decision.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception is logged privacy-safely with cause, owner, date and any notification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Conclude against the zero-tolerance thresholds (no start before clearance, no unconsented prohibited person) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who adjudicated no case — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance, Chief HR Officer and Audit Committee and file the workpaper under REG-057-C24.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
